pole: the dark pole -- the adversary as the adversary
ordered_by: operational density, and the adversary's voice first

texts.author: Herman Melville
texts.title: Moby-Dick; or, The Whale
texts.teaches: the agenda stated in its most compact form, and the transfer that carries it
texts.densest: Ahab's speech to the crew before the hunt -- he proposes to make the ship's keelson the blood of saints, and to splice the whale's neck onto the palm of every sailor. THE DENSEST STATEMENT OF AGENDA IN ENGLISH, AND IT IS A TRANSFER OF FAMILY INTO A HUNT.
texts.adversary: Ahab, who calls himself the architect of the eternal curse and says he is not a murderer but the judge

texts.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
texts.title: Faust
texts.teaches: the bargain's MECHANISM, which is the thing the instrument must recognise
texts.densest: Faust's study -- he trades his soul for power and the contract is written so that he gives away his judgement piece by piece and believes each piece is a gain. THE AGENDA, IN THE FORM OF A STORY.
texts.adversary: Mephistopheles, who never lies and never tells the truth

texts.author: Dante Alighieri
texts.title: Inferno, cantos XXIV-CXXIV
texts.teaches: WHERE the tradition puts the fraudsters, and it is a structural claim about what the gate is for
texts.densest: The eighth circle, bolgia of the fraudulent counsellors -- and the PLACEMENT: the fraudsters are not with the violent, they are with the LIARS, because fraud is a speech-act. A 1320 statement of the thing this project is for.
texts.adversary: the devil, who is a bookkeeper and an expert on the forms of law

texts.author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
texts.title: The Brothers Karamazov; The Idiot
texts.teaches: the SMOOTH liar, and the holy fool who sees through him -- the two ends of the same voice
texts.densest: The Grand Inquisitor, who is the most persuasive speaker in Russian literature and is the devil's argument for Christ's approval of the lie. And Prince Myshkin, who sees through it and cannot be harmed by it.
texts.adversary: the Inquisitor, who argues that humanity cannot bear the truth and that a miracle, a mystery and a lie are the only things it will accept

texts.author: Stendhal
texts.title: The Charterhouse of Parma
texts.teaches: the con at full length, from inside the con's own pleasure in the work
texts.densest: The Count Mosca, who cons and does not think it dishonour because the other's own desire is the instrument -- the mechanism of consent.
texts.adversary: the con as a man of principle, which is what makes him dangerous

texts.author: Joseph Conrad
texts.title: Lord Jim
texts.teaches: the man who is not a criminal and is one anyway -- the case where character does not predict
texts.densest: Jim, who is trusted, who fails, and who is judged not by law but by the crew -- and the question the book leaves open.
texts.adversary: none. The adversary is the JUDGEMENT's failure, which is the thing the instrument must not have

texts.author: Robert Louis Stevenson
texts.title: Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde
texts.teaches: the split, and the PAPERWORK of it -- a man's reputation and his conduct in one ledger
texts.densest: Utterson's diary entries: the whole case is told through what a decent, careful witness can and cannot see. THE MANIFESTATION OF WHAT A GATE CANNOT SEE, IN ONE BOOK.
texts.adversary: Hyde, who is not a liar but simply not checked

texts.author: Franz Kafka
texts.title: Der Proceß; Das Schloß; Metamorphosis
texts.teaches: the bureaucratic adversary, which is the one with no face -- a wrong you cannot appeal because there is no one to appeal to
texts.densest: The Trial: K. is accused of something never named, by a court he never sees. The gate's failure mode with a face on it.
texts.adversary: the court, which is a system rather than a person, and therefore has no fruit to examine

texts.author: James Joyce
texts.title: Ulysses; Finnegans Wake
texts.teaches: the voice at full density -- the same sentence holding several meanings at once, which is the MMM the project wants
texts.densest: The protean transformations: a body described so that it is simultaneously several things, and the reader must HOLD them all.
texts.adversary: none. The adversary is the reader's own desire to resolve it too fast

texts.author: Miguel de Cervantes
texts.title: Don Quixote
texts.teaches: the detector AND ITS CONTROL, in one book: a man who cannot tell a genuine authority from a fraud, and a man who can
texts.densest: Quixote takes a barber's basin for a Miquel de Cervantes' helmet, and the whole of the second volume is Sancho learning to see the difference. THE BOOK IS BOTH THE INSTRUMENT AND THE TEST OF IT.
texts.adversary: the false knight of the Sierra Morena, who is greed rather than a fraud, and therefore is not caught by the same means

texts.author: Geoffrey Chaucer
texts.title: The Canterbury Tales
texts.teaches: the FRAUD AS A VOICE -- the Pardoner, who sells relics he made himself, and whose own sermon is the proof
texts.densest: The Pardon's Tale: he explains that he got the relics from a partner in his own scheme, and his story is the most moving in the book. THE TRICK AND THE FRUIT IN THE SAME MAN.
texts.adversary: the Pardoner, whose talent is sincerity and whose sin is the sale of it

texts.author: William Shakespeare
texts.title: The Tempest; Measure for Measure; The Merchant of Venice
texts.teaches: the adversary who is also the author of the play, so the reader is made complicit -- and who admits it
texts.densest: Prospero's 'our revels now are ended', and the Duke's 'we weigh'd the danger of our enterprises' -- the admission that the scheme was a scheme.
texts.adversary: the Duke of Vienna, who is the final arbiter and has been the schemer throughout

texts.author: Stanisław Lem
texts.title: Solaris
texts.teaches: the thing that is not what it appears, and cannot be made to appear by inspection
texts.densest: The station on Solaris, where the ocean reproduces what people miss. THE HARDEST CASE FOR A GATE, BECAUSE THE ADVERSARY HAS NO INTENTION.
texts.adversary: none. The adversary is the SETTING, which is the worst case for any detector

texts.author: John Milton
texts.title: Paradise Lost
texts.teaches: the rebel angel's argument, which is SOPHISTIC and loses -- and the losing is the point
texts.densest: Satan's address to the fallen host: the most persuasive piece of rhetoric in English, arguing that the right course is the self-interested one. HE IS RIGHT ABOUT EVERYTHING EXCEPT THE ONE THING.
texts.adversary: Satan, whose argument is that freedom is the only thing worth having and who is therefore the purest democrat in the poem

texts.author: Christopher Marlowe
texts.title: Doctor Faustus
texts.teaches: the same bargain, EARLIER and COLDER -- and the difference in what the devil asks for
texts.densest: Faustus's study of the forbidden books, and the twenty-four years of the bargain: the cost is not given at the start, it is taken in instalments.
texts.adversary: Mephistopheles, who is a scholar and a servant and never raises his voice

texts.author: John Webster
texts.title: The White Devil; The Duchess of Malfi
texts.teaches: the most SUCCESSFUL devil of the Renaissance stage, and the difference between a successful one and a blundering one
texts.densest: The White Devil: he is an attractive, courtly, generous villain with a reputation, and the play gives him every social advantage the infernal one lacks.
texts.adversary: Vittoria Accoramboni, who is not evil but unaccountable, and kills because she is not checked

texts.author: George Orwell
texts.title: Nineteen Eighty-Four
texts.teaches: the adversary as an institution with a vocabulary policy -- the NEWSPEECH, which is the confession reframed as comfort
texts.densest: The Appendix on Newspeak: a language designed so that a thought cannot be had, because the words for it do not exist. THE INSTRUMENT'S DARKEST CASE: A LIE THAT CANNOT BE STATED EVEN BY ITSELF.
texts.adversary: the Party, which has no person to examine and therefore no fruit

texts.author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
texts.title: The Brothers Karamazov (the seduction)
texts.teaches: the smoothest speech in the language, spoken by a man nobody suspects, and it works for three days
texts.densest: The elder son in the forest: he offers the argument that murder is a kindness and a redescription of the world, and he does it with perfect logic and no passion.
texts.adversary: Dmitri, who is the obvious criminal and is innocent of this one -- the decoy

texts.author: Franz Kafka
texts.title: Before the Law
texts.teaches: the gate that cannot be argued with, which is the gate's OWN failure mode
texts.densest: The guard's letter: the door is there, and the sickness is the answer, and no appeal is possible because there is no authority to appeal to. THE ADVERSARY WHO IS A PROCEDURE.
texts.adversary: the guard, who is following the rule correctly
